summary: **Shri Jishnu Barua, Chairperson Shri Ramesh Babu V., Member Shri Harish Dudani, Member Shri Ravinder Singh Dhillon, Member** Saudamini, Plot No. 2, Sector 29 Gurugram – 122 001. **... Respondent(s) Parties Present** : Ms. Swapna Seshadri, Advocate, PGCIL Shri Utkarsh Singh, Advocate, PGCIL Shri Venkatesh, Advocate, NHPC Shri Ashutosh Kumar Shrivastava, Advocate, NHPC Shri Akash Lamba, Advocate, NHPC Shri Adarsh Singh, Advocate, NHPC Shri Aman Mahajan, NHPC Shri Zafrul Hassan, PGCIL Shri Angaru Naresh Kumar, PGCIL Shri Ranjeet Pandey, PGCIL Shri Ashish Alankar, PGCIL Shri Arjun Malhotra, PGCIL Ms. Kirti, PGCIL The instant Petition has been filed by Power Grid Corporation of India Limited (hereinafter referred to as “the Petitioner”), a deemed transmission licensee, for the determination of transmission tariff under the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Terms and Conditions of Tariff) Regulations, 2019 (hereinafter referred to as “the 2019 Tariff Regulations”) of the period from COD to 31.3.2024 with respect to the following transmission assets under “North East – Northern/ Western Interconnector – I Project” (hereinafter referred to as “transmission project”) in the North-Eastern Region. _*The Petitioner has claimed the proposed COD for Asset-2 and Asset-3 under Regulation 5(2) of the_ 2019 Tariff Regulations, due to the delay in commissioning of the generation asset under the scope of NHPC. 4. The matter was heard on 20.11.2025. During the course of the hearing, the learned counsel for the Petitioner requested the Commission to grant an interim tariff of 80% for the instant transmission assets, due to huge expenditure already incurred. 5. The Respondent, NHPC, has filed its reply vide affidavits dated 24.6.2025 and 15.9.2025, and the Petitioner has filed rejoinders vide affidavit dated 8.7.2025 and 22.9.2025. 6. We have considered the Petitioner’s submissions and prayer for the grant of an interim tariff. The rival contentions will be considered only at the time of the final tariff order. Therefore, the same are not deliberated in the instant interim order. _“In case the transmission system or element thereof executed by a transmission licensee is ready for commercial operation but the interconnected generating station or the transmission system of other transmission licensee as per the agreed project implementation schedule is not ready for commercial operation, the transmission licensee may file petition before the Commission for approval of the date of commercial operation of such transmission system or element thereof.”_ 8. As we are not deliberating in detail in this interim order, the prayer for the grant of COD under Regulation 5(2) of the 2019 Tariff Regulations shall be considered in the final order. _(3) If the information furnished in the petition is in accordance with these regulations and is adequate for carrying out prudence check of the claims made, the Commission may consider granting interim tariff in case of new projects._ _(5) The Commission shall grant final tariff in case of existing and new projects, after considering the replies received from the respondents, and suggestions and objections, if any, received from the general public and any other person permitted by the Commission including the consumers or consumer associations._ _(6) The Commission may hear the petitioner, the respondents and any other person permitted including the consumers or consumer associations while granting interim or final tariff._ _(7) The difference between the tariff determined in accordance with clauses (3) and (5) above and clauses (4) and (5) above, shall be recovered from or refunded to, the beneficiaries or the long term customers, as the case may be, with simple interest at the rate equal to the bank rate prevailing as on 1st April of the respective year of the tariff period, in six equal monthly instalments._ 10. As the Petitioner has filed the application in pursuance of Regulation 9(1) of the 2019 Tariff Regulations for the grant of interim tariff for its new transmission project under Regulation 10(3) of the 2019 Tariff Regulations, this interim tariff is being granted to the Petitioner after carrying out a preliminary prudence check of the Annual Fixed Cost (AFC) claimed by the Petitioner and taking into consideration the time over-run in case of the instant transmission assets, which shall be looked into in detail at the time of grant of the final tariff order. Accordingly, the interim tariff @ 70% of the AFC claimed in Asset-1 and Asset-4 in the instant Petition shall be allowed for the 2022-23 and 202324 tariff period in terms of Regulation 10(3) of the 2019 Tariff Regulations. However, the Commission is not inclined to allow an interim transmission tariff for Asset-2 and Asset-3 as the assets have not been put into commercial operation due to delay in commissioning of generation asset under the scope of NHPC, and the tariff has been claimed under Regulation 5(2) of the 2019 Tariff Regulations and hence, the same shall be dealt with in the final tariff order. 11. The Petitioner has claimed the following annual transmission charges with respect to the Asset-1 and Asset-4 for the 2019-24 tariff period: 12. Keeping in view, the expenditure already incurred by the Petitioner and due to non-commissioning of the downstream assets under the scope of NHPC, we hereby allow the Interim annual transmission charges only with respect to Asset-1 and Asset-4 are as follows: 13. The interim tariff allowed in this order shall be applicable from the COD of the transmission assets, and the billing, collection, and disbursement of the transmission charges approved in this order shall be governed by the provisions of the 2020 Sharing Regulations, as provided in Regulation 57 of the 2019 Tariff Regulations, as amended from time to time. Further, the interim transmission charges allowed in this order shall be subject to adjustment in accordance with Regulation 10 of the 2019 Tariff Regulations.
